question: A 32-year-old woman at 38 weeks gestation presents with a singleton fetus in persistent oblique lie. Which category best describes the indication for caesarean section in this case?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Non-reassuring CTG is a fetal indication, but this scenario describes an oblique lie, which is a mechanical / malpresentation indication, not a CTG abnormality.
CPD implies a size mismatch between head and pelvis. Oblique lie is a malpresentation — the baby is not presenting cephalically at all, so CPD does not apply here.
Correct. Oblique lie at term is an absolute indication for CS because vaginal delivery is impossible; the baby cannot pass through the pelvis in this position.
One previous LSCS is a relative indication for repeat CS (VBAC may be attempted in selected cases). A persistent oblique lie is a separate and more absolute indication here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the classification of LSCS indications: fetal (non-reassuring CTG, malpresentation), maternal (APH, previous uterine surgery), and combined. Oblique lie is a malpresentation.
Well done. Persistent oblique lie at term is a malpresentation — an absolute obstetric indication for caesarean section regardless of scar history.
